subject: Game Theory
title: Social Norms
description: A quick, practical guide to Social Norms.

hook.text: In Japan, nobody jaywalks even on empty streets. No cops, no fine. Just a norm so strong nobody breaks it.

buildup.text: Social norms are unwritten rules enforced by approval, gossip, and shame. They're cheaper than laws.

discovery.text: Cristina Bicchieri showed norms have two parts: people believe others follow the rule and believe others expect them to.

twist.text: Norms can flip fast. Smoking went from glamorous to shameful in one generation once the social expectation shifted.

climax.text: Development agencies now use norm-shifting instead of laws to fight child marriage, corruption, and littering.

punchline.text: The strongest rules are the ones nobody wrote.

quiz.question: What makes social norms powerful?
options: Beliefs about what others do and expect
